correctness.rationale: Splitting the two-color generating product at part size 128 and extracting a residue gives V_r(z) B(z)/(1-z)^14. The mod-8 functional equation for T^2 and P/(1-z^8) has a unique solution with constant 1 because each positive-degree coefficient depends only on earlier ones. The checked polynomial identities give V_r(z) B(z)/(1-z)^14 = 112/(1-z) modulo 128 for r=36,62: division is by units and multiplication by 112 carries the mod-8 identity to mod 128. Independent unbounded coin-change updates through index 224 leave exactly 36,62,96 at n=0 and rule out 96 at n=1. Legendre's theorem applies since each affected count is 16 times an integer congruent to 7 mod 8. The two progressions are disjoint and have combined density 1/64.
residual_risks: The computation verifies finite certificates and the finite exclusion, not the unbounded congruence by sampling; that congruence is obtained by the formal-series argument. No exact density of the full obstruction set is asserted.

value.rationale: Evaluated as mathematics, modulus 128 is natural here: valuation four plus the odd part modulo eight is exactly the Legendre obstruction at that valuation. Exhausting all aligned progressions at that modulus and producing a positive-density obstruction for two colors gives more than a sample congruence or a valuation check. This intrinsic value is not a claim of new contribution in light of the exact published overlap.
residual_risks: This is not a classification at other valuations or moduli, and the 1/64 bound is not the strongest indexed bound.
